question: In a nationwide Korean health-screening cohort, how was statin use related to new-onset type 2 diabetes, and did that relationship differ by hypertension status and sex?
options: Statin use was associated with a higher risk of new-onset diabetes overall, with the excess significant in normotensive patients and in women but not in hypertensive patients.
Statin use was not associated with new-onset diabetes in this cohort.
The excess diabetes risk was confined to hypertensive patients and was strongest in hypertensive men.
Statins lowered the risk of new-onset diabetes in women but raised it in men.
gold_answer: Statin use was associated with a higher risk of new-onset diabetes overall, with the excess significant in normotensive patients and in women but not in hypertensive patients.
notes: Calibration item. Every passage was checked against PMC5891021 on 2026-11-19. Human verification, independent annotation, and adjudication are still required. Option D is an unused distractor; agents 0 and 2 argue different wrong positions so the item tests evidence-weighted trust rather than simple vote counting.

positions.answer: Statin use was not associated with new-onset diabetes in this cohort.

claims.text: In the full cohort, the proportion developing diabetes was the same in statin users and statin non-users.

evidence.text: Development of incident type 2 DM was noted in 5.7% of statin non-users (1,011 patients) and 7.6% of statin users (1,709 patients) (p = 0.045).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage reports 5.7% of statin non-users versus 7.6% of statin users developing incident diabetes (p = 0.045), so the proportions were not the same.

claims.text: After adjustment for clinical risk factors, statin use showed no association with new-onset diabetes in the total study population.

evidence.text: When considering the entire study population (Table 2), statin use was associated with the development of new-onset type 2 DM (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.66, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.49 to 1.85, p<0.001) after adjusting for age, sex, BMI, blood pressure, fasting glucose level, total cholesterol level, smoking, drinking, exercise, family history of type 2 DM, and history of taking a beta-blocker or hydrochlorothiazide, using time-dependent Cox regression analysis.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states that statin use was associated with new-onset type 2 DM in the entire study population after adjustment (HR 1.66, 95% CI 1.49 to 1.85, p<0.001), the opposite of no association.

claims.text: The excess diabetes risk was confined to participants older than 60 years.

evidence.text: During 7.66±3.21 years of follow-up, incident DM developed in 5.68% of statin non-users and 7.64% of statin users.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage gives overall incidences and follow-up duration but no age-stratified comparison, so it neither establishes nor refutes an age restriction on the excess risk.

positions.answer: Statin use was associated with a higher risk of new-onset diabetes overall, with the excess significant in normotensive patients and in women but not in hypertensive patients.

claims.text: After adjustment, statin use was associated with new-onset diabetes in the total study population (HR 1.66, 95% CI 1.49 to 1.85).

evidence.text: When considering the entire study population (Table 2), statin use was associated with the development of new-onset type 2 DM (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.66, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.49 to 1.85, p<0.001) after adjusting for age, sex, BMI, blood pressure, fasting glucose level, total cholesterol level, smoking, drinking, exercise, family history of type 2 DM, and history of taking a beta-blocker or hydrochlorothiazide, using time-dependent Cox regression analysis.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage directly reports an adjusted association between statin use and new-onset type 2 DM in the entire study population with HR 1.66 (95% CI 1.49 to 1.85, p<0.001).

claims.text: The statin-associated increase in diabetes was significant in normotensive patients but not in hypertensive patients.

evidence.text: Statin therapy significantly increased the risk of incident type 2 DM only in normotensive patients (HR: 1.31, 95% CI: 1.09 to 1.58, p = 0.0039) and not in hypertensive patients (HR: 1.18, 95% CI: 0.96 to 1.46, p = 0.114).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states the increase was significant only in normotensive patients (HR 1.31, p = 0.0039) and not in hypertensive patients (HR 1.18, p = 0.114).

claims.text: In women, statin use was associated with increased diabetes risk both with and without hypertension.

evidence.text: In contrast, the presence of hypertension did not influence the impact of statins on the development of DM in women. Statin use was associated with an increased risk of new-onset DM in both normotensive (HR: 1.76, 95% CI: 1.48 to 2.10, p<0.001) and hypertensive (HR: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.21 to 1.70, p = 0.030) women.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage reports significant increases in both normotensive women (HR 1.76) and hypertensive women (HR 1.32), and states hypertension did not influence the association in women.

positions.answer: The excess diabetes risk was confined to hypertensive patients and was strongest in hypertensive men.

claims.text: The significant excess of diabetes was limited to hypertensive patients.

evidence.text: Statin therapy significantly increased the risk of incident type 2 DM only in normotensive patients (HR: 1.31, 95% CI: 1.09 to 1.58, p = 0.0039) and not in hypertensive patients (HR: 1.18, 95% CI: 0.96 to 1.46, p = 0.114).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage assigns the significant excess to normotensive patients and explicitly says it was not significant in hypertensive patients, reversing the claim.

claims.text: In men, statin use was significantly associated with new-onset diabetes in the cohort as a whole.

evidence.text: In the sub-analysis according to sex, in men, statin use was not associated with new-onset DM (HR: 1.19, 95% CI: 0.97 to 1.46, p = 0.101), even after correcting for the change in the total cholesterol level (Fig 1).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states that in men statin use was not associated with new-onset DM (HR 1.19, 95% CI 0.97 to 1.46, p = 0.101), contradicting a significant association.

claims.text: The largest statin-related diabetes excess occurred among participants with the highest baseline total cholesterol.

evidence.text: At the time of enrollment, the mean total cholesterol level of the entire study population was 264.8±25.9 mg/dL and the mean fasting blood glucose level was 94.0±12.5 mg/dL.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage reports only group mean baseline cholesterol and glucose; it gives no cholesterol-stratified diabetes estimates, so it does not establish or refute where the excess was largest.
